ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, and a downward-slanting straight line intersects a hyperbola. Point B is located on the hyperbola branch in the second quadrant, and point A is located on the hyperbola branch in the fourth quadrant, which is consistent with the positions of A(2,-3) and B(n,2) in the problem statement. Reasoning: Because A(2,-3) is on the hyperbola y=m/x, m=2×(-3)=-6. Also because B(n,2) is also on the hyperbola, 2=-6/n, solving gives n=-3, that is B=(-3,2). The straight line passes through A(2,-3) and B(-3,2), the slope k=(-3-2)/(2-(-3))=-1, substituting point A gives -3=-2+b, so b=-1, and the straight line is y=-x-1. It is required to solve kx+b>m/x, that is -x-1>-6/x, moving terms gives -x-1+6/x>0, which is transformed into -(x+3)(x-2)/x>0. The critical points are x=-3,0,2, and doing sign analysis gives that the intervals where the inequality holds are x<-3 or 0<x<2.

method.method_draft: Algebraic route. First read from the image that A is on the fourth-quadrant branch and B is on the second-quadrant branch, consistent with the line and hyperbola intersecting at the two labeled points. From the text, use A(2,-3) on y=m/x to get m=2·(-3)=-6. Since B(n,2) is also on the hyperbola, solve 2=-6/n to get n=-3, so B=(-3,2). Then determine the line through A(2,-3) and B(-3,2): slope k=(-3-2)/(2-(-3))=-1 and intercept b=-1, so the line is y=-x-1. Solve the inequality -x-1>-6/x by moving to one side: (-x-1)+6/x>0, i.e. -(x+3)(x-2)/x>0. Use the critical points x=-3,0,2 to make a sign chart and obtain x<-3 or 0<x<2.
